The '''1998 Decipher World Championship''' was the 3rd Star Wars CCG World Championship. Play was Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 November at the Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia.<ref name="pkt">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf 1998 World Championship packet], Decipher / Kendrick Summers (20 November 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195330/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> Decipher's packet is dated 20 November 1998 over [[Kendrick Summers]]' letterhead. The field was 56 finalists, including more than ten players from earlier World Finals. They qualified through named [[SWCCG regions]] and Open events.<ref name="pkt" /><ref name="insider43">Ryan Morris, "The Thrill of Victory", ''Star Wars Insider'' #43, pp. 64–65. Scan: [https://archive.org/details/starwarsinsider_1_to_153_plus_specials Star Wars Insider Magazines (1 to 153 + Specials)], Internet Archive. Facebook photographs, Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016012404/https://swccg.com/snapshots/facebook/insider-1998-worlds-p64.html Internet Archive] (p. 64); [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016012452/https://swccg.com/snapshots/facebook/insider-1998-worlds-p65.html Internet Archive] (p. 65)</ref>

This was the first constructed Worlds to use [[Special Edition]] before the public street date. Each finalist received a complete set of the expansion to build from.<ref name="insider43" /> [[Trandosite]] later called the weekend the Operative Worlds.<ref name="trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]].</ref>

[[Matt Potter]] of Duluth, Minnesota, defeated [[Michael Riboulet]] (United Kingdom) 2 (+9) and became the first American World Champion.<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref><ref name="insider43" /><ref name="trando" /> Riboulet became the first player in two Grand Finals.<ref name="trando" /> Potter qualified through [[SWCCG regions#Bespin|Bespin]] St. Charles; Riboulet through [[SWCCG regions#Kiffex|Kiffex]] Euro GenCon from Bristol.<ref name="pkt" />

The grand prize was an all-expense paid trip and VIP pass to Star Wars Celebration in Denver, 30 April–2 May 1999. The site was the Wings Over the Rockies Air and Space Museum.<ref name="insider43" /> The winner also received Japanese [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] and [[A New Hope]] full sets.<ref name="c1g">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/star-wars-worlds-1998/ Star Wars Worlds 1998], Category One Games (30 July 2013). Photographs and memories: [[Hayes Hunter]]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250115153905/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/star-wars-worlds-1998/ Internet Archive].</ref> [[Philipp Jacobs]], the 1997 World Champion, received a special invitation and did not have to qualify.<ref name="insider43" /><ref name="pkt" />

The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Special Edition]]. Packet structure (see [[Tournaments#1998 World Championship packet]]): Saturday Swiss, 4 rounds / eight games, top twelve advance. Those twelve may change decks Saturday night only. Sunday the twelve restart at 0 for four 60-minute games; top two play a two-game final. Everyone outside the twelve plays Sunday sealed. Highest total from Sunday's four games set allegiance for the first game of the final. Players handed in a deck list Saturday morning before play, and again Sunday morning if they reached the twelve. Players were to be prepared by 7:45am.<ref name="pkt" />

== Results ==

Places 1–4 per ''Star Wars Insider'' #43 and Trandosite; 5–12 are the rest of the final twelve as listed on Trandosite, whose Sunday order was not published; 13th and 14th per John Shields's interview and Trandosite.<ref name="insider43" /><ref name="trando" /><ref name="shields" /> Potter's Dark list on SWCCGDB / Trandosite is the '''day one''' Operatives deck.

=== Top 8 bracket ===

There was no elimination bracket. On Sunday the twelve restarted at 0 for four 60-minute games, and the top two played a two-game final; the highest total from Sunday's four games set allegiance for the first game of the final.<ref name="pkt" />

==== Championship match ====

Riboulet won the first game of the final by 19 with Dark Operatives. Potter won the second by 28, also on Operatives, retrieving a large amount of cards in the last seconds. Potter won 2 (+9).<ref name="trando" /><ref name="insider43" />

== Day 2 ==

On Sunday the twelve restarted at 0. Hernandez of Oregon led the remaining four with three wins. He played Riboulet for a place in the two-game final; Potter played [[Stuart Jones]] of Australia for the other place. The finalists were Potter and Riboulet.<ref name="insider43" /><ref name="trando" />

== Day 1 ==

Matching [[Operatives]] with [[Imperial Occupation / Imperial Control]] and [[Local Uprising / Liberation]] defined the weekend.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="insider43" /> On Saturday [[Tomoya Suzuki]] led the field, with [[Lucas Hernandez]] just behind. [[Evan Ferguson]] finished 14th, the highest finisher who did not play Operatives. [[Philipp Jacobs]] just missed the twelve; Riboulet made it.<ref name="trando" />

Friday night's banquet in the Cavalier showed the Episode I trailer, released to the public a few days earlier. Saturday play used 28 tables with country flags, news computers, and web cameras. After the final, [[Carol Wisely]], Decipher's Vice-President of Marketing, awarded medals as John Williams music played, and [[Warren Holland]] shook hands.<ref name="insider43" />

== Operatives ==

Potter's day-one Dark list is 20 [[Eriadu Operative]] under Imperial Occupation. His Light list is 20 [[Alderaan Operative]] under Local Uprising.<ref name="trando" />

After the event Decipher issued errata that hit [[Spaceport Speeders]] ([[Jon VanDerMeer]]'s timeout Light), then Operatives, [[Floating Refinery]], and [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]].<ref name="trando" /> Trandosite wrote that 1998 created more errata than Decipher had given out before.<ref name="trando" />

== Recollections ==

[[Chuck Kallenbach]] wrote in 2007 that [[Operatives]] were added late, with little in-house or remote playtesting, and that [[Joe Alread]] was among testers who flagged them. Decipher mailed [[Special Edition]] product to the finalists so the unreleased set could be used at Virginia Beach. Japanese testers asked for more Operative copies. A nor'easter kept players indoors that weekend. With no copy limit, Operative decks ran many copies of one card; players traded through Saturday night, including a 2 a.m. hall search. The design team did not change the rules mid-event. In the final, [[Tom Lischke]] asked Potter to recount a stack of cards; Potter won.<ref name="ck-worst">[https://iquotemyself.wordpress.com/2007/02/28/it-was-the-worst-of-times-period/ It was the Worst of Times. Period.], Chuck Kallenbach, i quote myself (28 February 2007). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20210719164120/https://iquotemyself.wordpress.com/2007/02/28/it-was-the-worst-of-times-period/ Internet Archive].</ref>

[[John Shields]] finished 13th. He said a missed Operative retrieval cost him 4 differential, enough for Sunday's twelve, and that others learned of Operatives about 2 a.m. after he had gone to bed.<ref name="shields">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026204829/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv10.htm John Shields interview], [[Trandosite]] (15 September 2000)</ref>

[[Matt Sokol]] won the [[SWCCG regions#Coruscant|Coruscant]] New York qualifier at 15 or 16 and flew to Virginia Beach with his mother. He met [[Hayes Hunter]] on a connecting flight. Decipher mailed a complete Special Edition set and boxes ahead of the event. Sokol playtested Operatives at home with [[Jonny Chu]] using five or six copies rather than twenty. He played Hunt Down and Hidden Base, went 4–4, and lost to every Operative opponent.<ref name="sokol-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jFXqTc1jkNc&t=1360s SWCCG PDS2: Matt Sokol, Worlds 2000 Champion Interview, HB X-wing Numbers, ISB Sandwhirl], BillBisco2 (6 May 2025), 22:40–28:40. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-jFXqTc1jkNc Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008224620/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jFXqTc1jkNc watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 8 October 2026).</ref>

Hunter, then 14, qualified through [[SWCCG regions#Kashyyyk|Kashyyyk]] Boston. His family went with him, including his brother [[Eric Hunter]]. Finalists received mailed Special Edition product. On Friday night players knocked on hotel doors trading toward twenty copies of one Operative for each side; Hunter slept through it on Hidden Base.<ref name="hunter-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=1813s SWCCG PDS2: Hayes Hunter Worlds 2023 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (10 May 2025), 30:13–32:30. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-qJuistFFk9M Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026).</ref>

Two weeks later, on 11 December 1998, [[Radio Free Decipher]] Broadcast 2 had [[Kendrick Summers]] with [[Jerry Darcy]], Lischke, and Kallenbach on a provisional Operatives ruling. They said Operatives had become a negative play experience, that they would errata rather than ban, and that they wanted the cards to remain a tournament strategy.<ref name="rfd2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w2Ao759YJlk&t=600s Radio Free Decipher Broadcast 2], Player's Council / Decipher (11 December 1998), 10:00–19:30. Host [[Kendrick Summers]]; guests [[Jerry Darcy]], [[Tom Lischke]], [[Chuck Kallenbach]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-w2Ao759YJlk Internet Archive].</ref>

Kallenbach later retold the mailed boxes and the late-night hall search for [[Kashyyyk Operative]] copies in a 2021 Booster Pack interview and a 2024 BoardMatt interview.<ref name="booster07">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BvVRth2CIwQ&t=2734s THE BOOSTER PACK #07 — Chuck Kallenbach PART 1], The Booster Pack Network (26 May 2021), 45:34–48:30. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016002120/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BvVRth2CIwQ Internet Archive] (watch page).</ref><ref name="boardmatt-ck">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=00zEbUKIGRQ&t=3820s Interview with Game Designer Chuck Kallenbach], BoardMatt (28 January 2024), 1:03:40–1:05:20. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-00zEbUKIGRQ Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20260227005313/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=00zEbUKIGRQ watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 27 February 2026).</ref>

Potter had playtested Operatives for more than a week.<ref name="c1g" />

== Format ==

The third official Worlds (56 finalists) shipped a paper packet dated 20 November 1998 over Kendrick Summers' (Marketing Manager) letterhead.<ref name="pkt" /> Its format page sets out Decipher Swiss at championship scale:

[[File:1998-worlds-p4.png|360px]]<ref name="pkt" />

'''Saturday 21 November''' — first stage, Decipher Swiss: 4 rounds / '''eight games''', random pairing at the start. Top '''twelve''' advance on victory points then differential. Saturday scores do '''not''' carry to Sunday. Those twelve "will be allowed to change their decks on Saturday night if they wish. This is the only time during the tournament that players may make adjustments to their decks." Everyone outside the twelve plays a Sunday sealed event instead.

'''Sunday 22 November''' — second stage: all twelve start at 0. Four 60-minute Swiss games, random pairing again. Top two on points then differential.

'''Final conflict''' — the top two start at 0 again. Two games (each player uses light and dark). Highest total from Sunday's four games sets allegiance for the first game of the final. Highest total from the two final games is 1998 World Champion. If still tied on points and differential, one extra game with allegiance randomized.

'''Sunday sealed''' (the rest of the field): four 45-minute Swiss games, then a winner-take-all between the top Dark and top Light. Earlier sealed scores do not carry into that last game.

Players handed in a deck list Saturday morning before play, and again Sunday morning if they had reached the twelve. The Code of Conduct required a 60-card check and held decks at the scoring table during Saturday; Life Force activation (one card at a time off the Reserve Deck, with insert cards announced) was strictly enforced for the weekend.<ref name="pkt" />

The packet also includes a December 1998 Current Rulings supplement (Cane Adiss, Cloud City location layout, cloud sectors, Hunt Down). It closes with the Code of Conduct overview Summers promised in the cover letter.

[[File:1998-worlds-p1.png|260px]]<ref name="pkt" />

== Schedule ==

Friday 20 November: finalists check into the Cavalier 1:00am–6:00pm; reception 6:30–8:30pm in Ballroom C; Q&A 8:30–10:00pm in Ballroom B. Saturday 21 November: breakfast 6:30–8:30am; preliminary tournament 8:00am–6:00pm in Ballroom A; lunch buffet 12:00–2:00pm; banquet 7:00–10:00pm in Orion's Lounge (11th floor). Sunday 22 November: breakfast 6:30–8:30am; finals 8:00am–3:00pm in Ballroom A; sealed deck 8:00am–1:00pm in Ballroom B; lunch buffet 12:00–2:00pm; awards 3:15–3:45pm; departure 4:00pm.<ref name="pkt" />
